newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania dazzled by Miss Europe beauty pageant.
newsitem.headline: Albania dazzled by Miss Europe beauty pageant.

text.p: Tirana streets were deserted on Saturday evening as Albanians tuned in to watch Miss England, Marie-Claire Harrison, win the Miss Europe '96 crown against the unlikely backdrop of Albania's stern Palace of Congresses.
Albania, once ruled by a Stalinist regime that spurned Western frivolity, had never before staged an event of such glitz and glamour.

The 49th Miss Europe beauty pageant drew contestants from 35 countries to the off-white palace on Tirana's tree-lined main boulevard. A celebrity audience replaced the grey-suited apparatchiks who used to roam its corridors.
President Sali Berisha and Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi rubbed shoulders with international music stars the Gypsy Kings and former U.S. beauty queens.
Harrison, a 23-year-old professional model from Clitheroe in Lancashire, won $20,000 in prize money and a traditional folk costume from Tirana city council.
She accepted her crown from Miss Europe '95, Monika Zidkova of the Czech Republic, after impressing the judges in evening dress, swimwear and national costume.
Miss Belarus Elena Chtcherbak came second in the competition, which was beamed to 200 million viewers across Europe. Russian-born Miss Israel Kim Rasliakova was third.
Harrison revealed a keen interest in fencing, horse riding, acting, dancing and water sports. She listed her favourite foods as cheese and pasta and saw her future in acting or presenting.
"My ideal man is (rock star) Sting," she explained, to loud applause.
"I not only find him attractive but he also has a strong sense of character and has done a lot of work for the Amazon rain forests. That's something I have a deep concern for too."
The contest capped a two-week stay in Albania by the contestants, some of whom admitted to being a little nervous ahead of their visit.
Despite the few roads, primitive communication and poorly-maintained infrastructure, most were won over after touring the countryside and Albania's Adriatic coast.
"Next year I think I'll come for my holidays here," said American Tracy Kemble, Mrs Globe 96-97, who compered the pageant, choreographed by France's Jean-Paul Plouvier.
In a video-link with the United States, actor Jim Belushi, partly of Albanian ancestry, sent his greetings.

Outside the main competition Miss Germany, Miriam Ruppert, became Miss Internet 96, Miss Russia, Victoria Bogdanova, became Miss Friendship '96 and Miss Greece, Panagiota Nonie Dounia, took the Miss Gjallica title. Albanian company Gjallica was the main sponsor of the pageant.
